See the CPU bounds checkpoint for executable ARM64 emitter evidence and current runtime status. 2026-09-07 local multiplayer: adapter_describe() now reports max_controllers = kMaxLocalControllers (8), matching Settings::values.players[0..7] (NpadIdType::Player1..Player8 -- the underlying InputSetting array has 10 slots, but 8 and 9 back Handheld and Other, which Lucent never routes local controllers onto). adapter_load() connects and sets ControllerType::ProController on all 8 of those player slots before InitializeEmulation reloads HID devices (previously only players[0]), so a multiplayer session finds every controller_index adapter_set_control() will honor already connected at boot. adapter_set_control() gained the ABI v2 controller_index parameter (uint32_t, ahead of the control enum, matching the v2 header) and now calls VirtualGamepad::SetButtonState/SetStickPosition with that index instead of a hardcoded constexpr kPlayerOne = 0; any controller_index >= kMaxLocalControllers is a fail-closed no-op (dropped, never aliased onto player 0). Local patch to the vendored Eden tree, NOT an upstream contribution. java.lang.{Double,Integer,Boolean}.value are private fields carrying the max-target-p hidden-API restriction, so Android denies GetFieldID by JNI for any app targeting above API 28; Lucent targets 30. The denial leaves a pending NoSuchFieldError that JNI_OnLoad never clears, so ART aborts the process before a title can boot. The patch clears that specific pending exception and logs it. Boxing still works because the constructors are public; only unboxing through the cached field is lost, and Lucent never drives Eden's Java settings path. Behaviour on API<=28 is unchanged, since the lookup succeeds there and there is nothing to clear.

Local patch to the vendored Eden tree, NOT an upstream contribution. Lucent owns the audio device: the adapter ABI hands every engine an audio_sink backed by a Lucent AudioTrack, so Eden must render into that and must NOT open a device of its own. Eden picks its backend from a constexpr table keyed on Settings::AudioEngine, and there is no enumerator meaning 'the embedding host owns the device'; adding one would have to touch the enum, its canonicalizations, its metadata specializations and the Qt settings UI. The patch instead adds a single file-local factory pointer plus SetLucentSinkFactory(), consulted at the top of CreateSinkFromID. The adapter installs it before InitializeEmulation and clears it on stop; when it is null the file behaves exactly as upstream. Taking over the sink rather than tapping it is deliberate: it keeps Eden's own down-mix, volume and buffer-release accounting, and it stops OboeSink from being constructed at all -- OboeSinkStream is destroyed through Sink::CloseStream while its OpenSL ES buffer-queue callback is still registered, and neither Oboe's destructors nor Eden ever call oboe::AudioStream::close(), which is a use-after-free on a platform audio thread every time a guest ends an audio session.

Local defensive replacement in the vendored Eden tree, NOT an upstream contribution and NOT yet a device-proven fix. AArch64 DWARF for the prior object places Event::handle at 0x28 (the weak_ptr begins at 0x10 and its control pointer is at 0x18), correcting the earlier lock note. The retained stacks prove an invalid/damaged fibonacci-heap node but lack the faulting PC/registers needed to prove whether the 0x28 fault was the Event handle load or an inlined null Boost-node access. The old source did retain const Event& across basic_lock.unlock(), but its sequence-number guard handles the direct same-type-unschedule path, so that alone is not a complete causal explanation. This replacement makes the invariant structural: Advance copies and pops the due node before unlocking, no queue reference or handle survives the callback window, a looping event is freshly emplaced only when its sequence is unchanged, and Event no longer stores a self-referential handle at all (UnscheduleEvent derives handles from locked iterators through Boost's public s_handle_from_iterator API). Expired weak events are popped as well, avoiding the upstream infinite loop. Deterministic native tests cover concurrent NoWait cancellation during a blocked callback, removal of 256 same-type entries, and expired-event consumption; the required device gate remains three consecutive clean ten-minute gameplay runs.

Local patch to the vendored Eden tree, NOT an upstream contribution. System::Impl::ShutdownMainProcess closed the HLE services AFTER suspending emulation. Eden's services are not host threads: Services' constructor starts each one through KernelCore::RunOnGuestCoreProcess, which creates a KProcess and a KThread pinned to guest core 3 and runs ServerManager::LoopProcess on it. KernelCore::SuspendEmulation walks GetProcessList() and requests SuspendType::System on every thread of every process, so it parks those service threads, and KernelCore::CloseServices then destroys the ServerManagers, whose destructor does an unbounded m_stopped.Wait() for the thread it just parked to run its loop out. That is suspend-then-wait-for-the-suspended. It is intermittent because KThread::TrySuspend declines to park a thread that still has kernel waiters, so whether a given service thread is parked in time is a race -- which is why most Switch exits tear down in under a second and some wedge forever with kernel.CloseServices as the last step reached. The patch closes the services first and suspends afterwards; nothing between the two relies on the guest being parked, and the following ShutdownCores/TerminateAllProcesses force-clears suspension itself. After the kernel and every guest-memory owner have shut down, it also resets DeviceMemory: upstream expects the Android process to end after a title, while EmuFusion keeps one process alive and otherwise retained more than 4 GiB of committed guest memory plus a stale address-space tracker after held Stop. ReinitializeIfNecessary recreates DeviceMemory for the next title. The file also carries LOG_INFO teardown step markers through ShutdownMainProcess, which localised both problems and keeps the next teardown failure diagnosable from logcat alone.

patches.note: Android's ASSERT is logging-only in this tree. The old HostMemory Map/Unmap/Protect code asserted that virtual_offset + length fit, then continued into the placeholder tracker and MAP_FIXED even when teardown supplied an already-retired range beyond the 39-bit reservation. Every held-Stop therefore emitted a second invalid mmap and an Out of memory critical line. This patch uses overflow-safe subtraction bounds and returns before touching the placeholder map or mmap/mprotect. Guest-memory lifetime itself is handled by the System::Impl DeviceMemory reset recorded in core.cpp, instead of layering a partial page-discard operation onto HostMemory.

Local fail-closed bounds patch, source-proven from the Thor Blasphemous II tombstone. Maxwell's tracker owns exactly a 34-bit top_tier table, but both range walkers derived page_index from a caller-provided DAddr and indexed top_tier before checking the aperture. Android logging assertions do not stop execution, so a stale or malformed range produced an arbitrary Manager pointer and crashed in WordManager::IsRegionModified. Both walkers now stop before any out-of-aperture access; this rejects the invalid suffix without relaxing GPU accuracy or masking an in-range tracker defect.
